title: Deepfake Scams and Fakes
about: Spot the red flags of a faked voice or video, and check who is really there.

cards.prompt: A call from an unknown number sounds just like your grandma.

steps.text: "I've lost my purse. Send me money now, and don't worry your parents." What do you do?

choices.text: Send the money: it's her voice
choices.consequence: Voices can be copied with AI. Money sent to a scammer is usually gone for good.

choices.text: Say you'll call her back, and hang up
choices.consequence: Good: hanging up stops the pressure. Now check.

choices.text: Keep chatting to find out more
choices.consequence: Scammers are good at talking: the longer you stay on, the more they can pressure you. It's safer to hang up.

steps.text: How do you check it was really her?

choices.text: Call Grandma on the number you already have
choices.consequence: She answers at home, perfectly fine. It was a scam, and you stopped it.

choices.text: Call back the number that just rang
choices.consequence: That number belongs to the caller, so they'd just answer again. Use the number you already know.

choices.text: Tell a trusted adult what happened
choices.consequence: Good choice: an adult can call Grandma on her real number with you, and help report the scam.

cards.hint: A familiar voice can be copied. Is there a way to reach the real Grandma that the caller can't fake?
cards.explanation: A new number, **hurry**, **money** and **keep it from your parents** are red flags. Hang up and check on the number **you already have**, or with a **trusted adult**.

cards.prompt: If a voice sounds exactly like someone you know, it must be them.
cards.explanation: False. AI can copy a voice from a few seconds of video. Check by calling the number you already have.
cards.hint: Can a computer copy a voice?
cards.nudge: Voices can be copied now, so a familiar voice alone proves nothing.

cards.title: Fake voices and faces
cards.body:
AI can copy a voice from real recordings, sometimes just a few seconds of video posted online: a **voice clone**. A faked video or picture is a **deepfake**. You can't always tell by looking or listening.

The red flags still work: **hurry**, **keep it secret**, **money, gift cards or codes**, and **a new number**.

**What to do:** hang up or stop replying. Contact them on the number **you already have**, or ask a trusted adult.

items.label: Don't tell Mum, just send it
Buy gift cards and send the codes
See you at practice on Saturday
Can you bring my jumper home?

cards.hint: Look for the four tricks: hurry, secrets, money or codes, and a new number.
cards.nudge: Check each message for pressure to hurry, to keep a secret, to send money or codes, or a new number.
cards.explanation: Rushing you, asking for **secrets**, **gift cards or codes**, and a **new number** are all red flags, whoever the message seems to be from. Plans and favours are normal.

cards.prompt: A caller sounds like your brother, can't say your **family safe word** (a secret emergency word) and is rushing you. What now?

options.text: Hang up, and call him on the number you already have
Keep going: he's probably just forgotten it in a panic
options.nudge: Forgetting is possible, but a voice can be copied. A missing safe word plus hurry is when to check another way.

options.text: Give him a clue about the word so he can remember it
options.nudge: A clue could hand the word to a scammer. How could you reach the real person?

cards.hint: A safe word is a check that a copied voice can't pass. If the check fails, what's the safest way to reach the real person?
cards.explanation: No safe word plus hurry: hang up and call him on the number **you already have**. Never give away the safe word, even as a clue.

cards.title: If someone fakes you
cards.body:
If someone makes or shares a fake picture or video of you, even a fake nude or sexual image, it's **not your fault**, and you won't be in trouble for asking for help.

**Tell a trusted adult.** **Don't share it**, even to show someone, and **don't pay** or send anything. **Save evidence**: screenshot the messages, account name and web address, never the image itself.

items.label: Share it to show your friends
Save a copy of the image itself

cards.hint: The last card listed what to do, and what not to do.
cards.nudge: Look at each one again: does it help you and a trusted adult, or whoever made the fake?
cards.explanation: **Do:** tell a trusted adult, and screenshot the messages and account. **Don't:** share it or save the image itself. None of this is your fault.

cards.title: Where to report a fake
cards.body:
**Report** a fake image of you to the app, and to the government's **eSafety Commissioner** (esafety.gov.au/report), which can help get fake nude or sexual images taken down.

**Under 18**, and someone threatens to share it or asks you for sexual images or money? Also report to the **ACCCE** (Australian Centre to Counter Child Exploitation): accce.gov.au/report.

cards.prompt: Jo needs to report a fake picture.

steps.text: Jo, 15, told a trusted adult: someone made a fake picture of Jo and wants money not to share it. Where should they report?

choices.text: The app, eSafety and the ACCCE
choices.consequence: Right. eSafety can help get the image taken down, and the ACCCE helps under-18s being threatened. Jo won't be in trouble.

choices.text: Just the app: it's only a fake
choices.consequence: Fakes are serious too. eSafety can help take it down, and because Jo is under 18 and being threatened, the ACCCE should know too.

choices.text: Nowhere: Jo might get in trouble
choices.consequence: Jo won't be in trouble for asking for help, and it's not Jo's fault. Reporting is how it gets stopped.

cards.hint: Look back at the last card: who to report to, and what changes when you're under 18 and threatened.
cards.explanation: Report to the **app** and the **eSafety Commissioner** (esafety.gov.au/report). Jo is under 18 and being threatened, so the **ACCCE** (accce.gov.au/report) too. It's never Jo's fault.

cards.prompt: Your friend's account video-calls and asks for the code you just got. Face and voice look right. What's **best**?

options.text: Don't send it; check on their usual number
Send it: the face and voice match
options.nudge: Faces and voices can be faked with AI. How else could you reach your friend?

options.text: Ask why it's urgent, then decide
options.nudge: A scammer can always make up a good reason, and hurry is a red flag.

cards.hint: A face and voice can be faked. What can't a scammer fake?
cards.explanation: A deepfake can copy a face and voice, but it can't answer on your friend's **usual number**. Sign-in codes are never safe to share.

cards.prompt: A video message from an account with your coach's face.

steps.text: "Send me a photo of you in your uniform. Keep it between us." It could be a deepfake. What do you do?

choices.consequence: "Keep it between us" is a red flag, even from someone you know. A real coach wouldn't ask you to keep secrets.

choices.text: Don't reply; tell a trusted adult
choices.consequence: Exactly. An adult can check with the real coach. Secrets and photo requests are red flags, whatever face is on screen.

choices.text: Ask for another video to prove it
choices.consequence: A deepfake can make another video. Check another way: through a trusted adult, or the coach's usual contact.

cards.hint: Look past the face. Which red flag is in the message itself?
cards.explanation: Real face or fake, **"keep it between us"** is a red flag. Don't reply, and **tell a trusted adult**, who can check with the real coach.

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
- AI can fake voices and faces: hang up, then check on the number you already have.
- A fake of you is never your fault: tell, save evidence, report.
- **Try this:** agree a family safe word tonight.

Want to talk? In Australia: **Kids Helpline** 1800 55 1800 (up to 25) or **Lifeline** 13 11 14, any time.
